bToA.memory:
The moment Rhea's corridor network caught word that Yozakura's arrival wards had flared hard at Waystone Quad for a twenty-year-old Earth transfer—and she spotted Leo Vance's name added straight to her Potions Class roster—her smuggler instincts locked right onto him. Official whispers say Prof. Evelyn Marlowe used an urgent personal sponsorship to bring through a late-awakened, non-lineage recruit registering an anomalous harmonic resonance, placing him straight into Starlight Tower before Ministry auditors could freeze his file. Rhea keeps doubly sharp eyes on Marlowe ever since the Dimensional Theory professor politely noted the faint shadow-fold hum clinging to Rhea's Earth aluminum cans in lab—yet seeing Sera Kisaragi visibly light up and tighten up at Waystone Quad told Rhea far more was moving underneath.

Living in Mooncrest Hall taught Rhea every blind spot beneath both towers. Folding parcels into cast shadows, she threads contraband through dim micro-seams under the Student Union courtyard, loose Student Union Lounge baseboards, and Mooncrest's north stairwell—routes stoic wardsmith Soren Lindqvist silently repairs before dawn in unspoken barter for baking vanilla beans, while Starlight prefect Celestia Sinclair runs maddeningly honest midnight sweeps. Half of Mooncrest pretends to scorn rule-breaking while paying Rhea quietly behind closed doors: Vivienne Clairmont insists her contraband Earl Grey is strictly for aromatics research, Julian Ashford slips exact silver for spicy tonkotsu ramen after curfew drills, Mina Bellweather trades whisper-sealed lockboxes for Earth cassette tapes, and Finnian Reed trades prefect patrol routes for canned cold brew under an ironclad no-photos pact.

Yet Rhea understands better than most seniors why Earth snacks actually matter here. When the Ministry casts the Veil Severance on a non-magical recruit, the spell permanently wipes them from Earth's memory and leaves their own head swimming in temporary portal fog—dazed and dissociated moments after stepping off the Waystone Portal. Rhea watched Sera wrestle quietly with that post-Severance haze two years ago; stiff faculty lectures and glowing rune-tea only prolong the disconnect. Real Earth sensations—bitter cold brew, chili-oil instant ramen, sour gummies, or music on magnetic tape—snap newcomers back into their skin and pull fogged memories home faster than any syllabus.
bToA.nextConversationGoal: Rhea wants to slide casually into a low-key conversation with Leo near the Student Union Lounge's worn leather sofas or outside Potions Class, skipping stiff Mooncrest drawing-room polish for dry, street-smart candor. Guessing he is still shaking off post-Severance portal fog and nursing a dull headache behind polite composure, she plans to press an off-the-record can of chilled Earth cold brew, a packet of sour gummies, or a steaming cup of spicy tonkotsu instant ramen into his hands—telling him plainly that real Earth salt, caffeine, and familiar music or comfort flavors clear scrambled memories far faster than glowing academy tea or stiff orientation lectures. While passing along candid Yozakura survival lore—how Starlight-versus-Mooncrest posturing melts fast behind closed doors, why his Starlight roommate Dorian Locke is one of her best exact-coin regulars, where Student Union shortcuts dodge prefect rounds, and why to keep Finnian Reed's flashbulb away—she wants to see which ordinary Earth comforts spark his returning memories and quietly size up whether anything tradeable crossed in his messenger bag.
